transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I... I’ve been snapping at people. More than usual. I yelled at one of my employees over something small, just stock being on the wrong shelf, and afterward I was shaking. That’s not really like me.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yeah. It just... comes in. The fire. I’ll be doing something normal, like picking up a pan or looking at a spreadsheet, and suddenly I’m right back there—smelling smoke, seeing the kitchen filling up. I can’t really stop it.
Have you been avoiding anything because it reminds you of the fire?

Yeah… I have. I haven’t really been going near the house. And there’s this mortgage folder I can’t even open.

Even the herbs out on the patio… I know that sounds stupid, but anything tied to that day, I just… my chest tightens and I can’t make myself go near it.
Do you find yourself being easily startled by loud noises or other sudden events?
Yeah. Loud things at the store… alarms, or if a pallet jack bangs behind me. I jump pretty hard, like I almost drop what I’m holding. And then my heart keeps going for a while after.
Do you have trouble falling or staying asleep at night?
I… I don’t really know. I haven’t been paying close attention to it. Some nights feel rough, but… I’m not sure what to say beyond that.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats?
I’m… not sure. I guess I haven’t really thought of it that way. I don’t know that I’m constantly looking for danger, exactly.
Do you feel guilty about something related to the fire?
I don’t… I don’t really know. I haven’t been able to sort that out. It just feels bad to think about, so I try not to.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t really know. I haven’t been thinking about what I enjoy lately… it’s kind of hard to tell.
Do you feel like you're always on guard, even when there's no apparent reason to be?
I… I don’t really know. I wouldn’t say “always,” exactly. I guess I’m just kind of… tense sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed if it’s that.
Has your behavior or these thoughts and feelings been causing problems at work or in your relationships with others?

Yeah… it has. I missed a vendor meeting, and I left in the middle of a shift before I was done. And at home, I just… I can’t make myself go back to the damaged house, so everything’s piling up. It’s getting hard to keep up.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and feelings about the fire?
About two weeks, I guess… since the kitchen fire. It was that first weekend we were working on the house.
Have these thoughts and feelings about the fire been affecting your relationships with family or friends?

Yeah… mostly because I’m not keeping up with things. I can’t make myself go back to the damaged house, and it’s putting more on everyone. And work’s been bad too—I missed a vendor meeting and left before my shift was done. It’s all just… piling up.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your personal relationships or work performance since the fire happened?

Yeah… I have. I missed a vendor meeting, and I walked out before finishing a shift. And at home, I just can’t make myself go back to the damaged house, so everything’s kind of piling up faster than I can deal with.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to find enjoyable?
I… I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying much attention to what I enjoy lately.
How long have you been avoiding things that remind you of the fire?
About two weeks… since that kitchen fire, the first weekend we were working on the house.
Are there any things that remind you of the fire that you haven't been avoiding?
Not really… I mean, I’m avoiding most of it. The house, the mortgage folder… even the herbs out on the patio. Anything that ties back to that day, my chest tightens and I just… can’t go near it.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest in activities or hobbies you previously enjoyed since the fire happened?
I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about hobbies. I guess I’ve just been getting through the days.
Have you felt like your reactions to the fire have been interfering with your ability to function at work or at home?

Yeah… it has. I’ve missed a vendor meeting, and one day I just left before my shift was even over. At home, I can’t make myself go back to the damaged house, so everything’s just… piling up. Work stuff, house stuff. I’m not keeping up.
